text:
Anya: perf-bot flagged a regression in prefix cache hit-rate after the tokenizer update on canary. +4.2% misses 08:00-10:00. stack=dedicated-prod, model=redwood-3b-q4. Anyone seen warmup failures or weird tool-call noise?
perf-bot: nightly-run: prefix-cache miss +4.2% vs baseline. top diffs: tokenizer v1.3.1 -> v1.4.0, system_prompt normalization toggled, tool_field ordering change.
Drew: I rolled tokenizer yesterday to pick up a bugfix. Didn't expect cache churn. Did we change how function-call payloads get tokenized?
Kai: Yes, tokenizer now treats JSON object insertion as unordered by default (we optimized for dedup). That can reorder keys -> different token sequence -> different cache signatures.
Elaine: We rely on deterministic canonicalization when building cache keys. Tokenizer reorder = busted invariants. We should either pin tokenizer.version in the key or make serialization deterministic for the cache signature.
Anya: Quick mitigation: add `tokenizer.version` string to the cache signature and bump warmup TTL for the canary cohort. Also audit the canonicalizer for tool/function-call fields.
Drew: Adding tokenizer.version will cause churn on deploys (we'll lose warmed prefixes). Is that acceptable short-term?
Kai: It'll cause temporary churn but prevents incorrect hits. Another path: perform a tokenizer-stable serialization step used only for cache-key computation (independent of the tokenizer used for model inputs). For example: `stable_bytes = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(
,:
))`.
Elaine: We tried `sort_keys=True` before and it broke some ordered-tool semantics where field order encoded intent. We need to preserve intentional ordering for runtime.
Anya: Proposal: two-layer approach: 1) canonical prompt for runtime that preserves semantic ordering, 2) a tokenizer-stable serialization (deterministic) used exclusively for cache signature. That way cache keys don't flip when tokenizer changes, but runtime still sees ordered payloads.
Drew: That makes sense. Note: the cache miss amplified kernel routing to fallback pools which increased tail latency for affected requests. So this isn't just a cache hit-rate metric problem.
Kai: Implementation idea: add an opt-in `stable_key` annotation to function-call metadata. SDKs can populate it with a stable serialization hash if the client knows ordering semantics. Servers fallback to server-side deterministic serialization if the annotation is absent.
perf-bot: follow-up-run: patched canary with `tokenizer.version` in key + temp warmup TTL. Miss-rate rolled back to baseline in ~3h. Token cost increased ~2% during re-warm.
Elaine: Long-term: include `tokenizer_version` + `serialization_hash` in cache metadata and expose mismatch telemetry in Console (per-model, per-region). We should also surface which prefixes were invalidated on deploy.
Anya: Action items: Kai - draft proto for `stable_key` annotation and SDK contract (EOD). Drew - server PR to include `tokenizer.version` + stable serialization hash in key generation; add safe fallback path. Elaine - add alert in perf dashboard for prefix miss delta > 2% and a nightly diff job for warmup coverage by tokenizer/model.
Drew: I'll also add a nightly job that diffs warmup coverage by model + tokenizer version so we can quantify churn risk before rolling a tokenizer.
Kai: We should consider shard-level cache tagging so we can invalidate only affected shards/prefixes instead of evicting large swaths. I'll sketch that option in the proto.
Elaine: Good call. We'll discuss shard-tagging and rollout plan in tomorrow's arch sync.
Anya: Thanks everyone — small patch for canary landed, monitoring up. Please react with :eyes: when you've read the action items.
Drew: reading :eyes:
Kai: ack
Elaine: ack
perf-bot: noted: follow-up-run scheduled in 6h to check post-warm metrics.
